name: CHARM-II
summary: CHARM-II was a distinct successor detector at CERN, optimized for precision neutrino-electron scattering using a much larger and more finely segmented low-density target.
physics_targets: Weak mixing angle from purely leptonic scattering
Neutrino trident production and new interactions
detection_principle: Glass target plates alternated with streamer-tube tracking and scintillator planes. Fine shower-angle reconstruction selected the narrow forward electron signal, while an iron muon spectrometer characterized charged-current control samples.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: Historical apparatus and published data are documented by the cited experiment publications.

timeline.event: Detector assembled and exposed to CERN neutrino beams
Detailed calibration and detector performance publication

collaboration.name: CHARM-II Collaboration

key_parameters.name: Target calorimeter
key_parameters.value: Approximately 700 tonnes of glass-based sampling calorimetry

key_parameters.name: Segmentation
key_parameters.value: Glass plates about half a radiation length thick with streamer planes

key_parameters.name: Muon analysis
key_parameters.value: Downstream magnetized iron modules reused from CDHS

results.summary: Published measured detector response, electron/hadron discrimination and muon resolution supporting precision leptonic weak-interaction measurements.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
